title: A day with Pip
theme: Daily routines, time and days of the week

canDo: Say what I do every day and at what time
Say what I do on different days
grammar: present simple: I get up / she gets up
What time do you ...? At ... o'clock.

chunks.example: I get up at seven o'clock.
On Saturdays I go to the park.
What time do you go to bed?
After school I do my homework.
My mum drinks tea every day.

talkMissions.title: My morning
talkMissions.goal: Child describes her morning routine in order with times (get up, wash, breakfast, school). Pip compares with his Zoot routine (he gets up at night!) and asks 'What time do you ...?'.
talkMissions.opener: On Zoot, I get up at night and sleep in the day! It's very funny. What time do you get up?
hints: I get up at seven o'clock.
I go to school at eight.
What time do you get up, Pip?

talkMissions.title: My week
talkMissions.goal: Child talks about different days: school days vs weekend, one activity per day, using 'On Mondays I ...' and frequency words. Pip asks about her favourite day and why.
talkMissions.opener: On Zoot, there are no days, only one long day! On Earth you have Monday, Tuesday... What do you do on Saturdays?
hints: On Saturdays I go to the park.
I never get up early on Sunday!

talkMissions.title: Who does what?
talkMissions.goal: Child talks about family members' routines using he/she + verb-s (My dad drinks coffee, My mum works...). Pip recasts missing -s naturally. Pip also describes his sister Mimi's day.
talkMissions.opener: My sister Mimi gets up very early. She eats apples and she plays all day! What does your mum do every day?

letters.subject: My day on Earth
letters.body:
Dear friend,
Here is my day on Earth. I get up at seven o'clock. I wash my face and I brush my teeth. Then I have breakfast. I love toast and honey! In the morning I go to the park and I watch the birds. In the afternoon I read books about Earth. I go to bed at nine o'clock. What do you do every day?
Pip 🦊
letters.replyPrompt: Tell Pip about your day. What time do you get up? What do you do after school?
letters.replyPromptTr: Pip'e gününü anlat. Saat kaçta kalkıyorsun? Okuldan sonra ne yapıyorsun?

questions.q: What time does Pip get up?
What does Pip do in the afternoon?

letters.subject: Mimi's day
letters.body:
Dear friend,
My sister Mimi is on Zoot. She sends me a letter every week. Mimi gets up very early. She has breakfast with Mum. She goes to fox school. Her teacher's name is Mr Tok. After school she plays with her friends and she draws pictures. She never does her homework! Does your friend do her homework?
Pip 🦊
letters.replyPrompt: Tell Pip about a friend or a family member. What does he or she do every day?
letters.replyPromptTr: Pip'e bir arkadaşını ya da aileden birini anlat. O her gün neler yapıyor?

questions.q: What does Mimi do after school?

letters.subject: My favourite day
letters.body:
Dear friend,
I have a new favourite day. It is Saturday! On Saturdays there is no school for children. The park is full of children and dogs. I sometimes play ball with them. In the evening I eat chicken and chips. Yum! What is your favourite day? Why?
Pip 🦊
letters.replyPrompt: Tell Pip your favourite day and why. What do you do on that day?
letters.replyPromptTr: Pip'e en sevdiğin günü ve nedenini yaz. O gün neler yapıyorsun?

questions.q: What does Pip eat in the evening?

story.title: A day in my life
story.prompt: Make a comic: draw four moments of your day.
story.promptTr: Bir çizgi roman yap: gününden dört anı çiz.

pages.prompt: Morning: what do you do in the morning?
School: what do you do at school?
Afternoon: what do you do after school?
pages.promptTr: Öğleden sonra: okuldan sonra ne yapıyorsun?

explorer.title: Animals of the night
explorer.text: Some animals sleep in the day and wake up at night. We call them nocturnal animals. Owls, bats and foxes are nocturnal. They have got very good eyes or ears. Bats can't see well, but they can hear very well. They make a sound and listen. Then they know where things are!
facts: Nocturnal animals are awake at night.

explorer.title: How a clock works
explorer.text: A clock has got two hands. The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes. When the long hand is on twelve, we say "o'clock". There are sixty minutes in one hour and twenty-four hours in one day. Long ago, people used the sun to tell the time!
facts: The short hand shows the hour.
There are 60 minutes in an hour.
There are 24 hours in a day.

questions.q: What does the long hand show?
How many hours are in one day?
What did people use long ago?
